objects.taxonomy_description: Large wading bird measuring 120-145 cm in height with wingspan reaching 140-170 cm. Plumage ranges from pale pink to vivid scarlet depending on diet, with darker coloration on wings and tail. Neck is extremely elongated and S-curved, comprising approximately one-third of total body length. Bill is distinctive with downward-curving shape, deep black at tip transitioning to pale pink at base, adapted for filter-feeding. Legs are exceptionally long and bright pink to red with webbed feet. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with compact torso contrasting elongated neck and legs. Wings display black primary feathers visible during flight. Flight posture features full neck extension. Juveniles display grey-white plumage developing pink coloration over 2-3 years. Weight ranges 2-4 kg.

objects.taxonomy_description: Stringed instrument with solid or semi-hollow body (no sound hole required). Body shape varies: Stratocaster (double-cutaway, contoured edges), Les Paul (single-cutaway, carved top), Telecaster (single-cutaway, slab body). Body is wood (alder, mahogany, maple) with glossy polyester or nitrocellulose finish in solid colors, sunburst, or natural wood grain. Neck is maple or mahogany with fretted fingerboard (rosewood or maple, 21-24 frets). Pickups (magnetic, 1-3) mounted on body. Control knobs (volume, tone) and pickup selector switch. Bridge is fixed or tremolo. Headstock has 6 tuning pegs. Cable jack on body edge.

objects.taxonomy_description: Medium-sized freshwater to brackish water turtle measuring 12-25 cm in carapace length. Carapace is oval and moderately domed with a smooth surface; coloration varies from brown to olive with concentric growth rings visible on each scute. Some species exhibit ornate patterning with yellow or orange markings on dark scutes. Plastron is large and hinged, enabling partial closure. Head is moderately sized with a pointed snout and small eyes; skin coloration is grey to olive with distinctive striped or spotted patterning on the head and neck. Limbs are moderately long with webbed feet and sharp claws. Tail is short. The turtle exhibits a characteristic basking posture on logs or banks with limbs extended and head raised. Skin texture is smooth with fine scales. Adapted for both aquatic and terrestrial environments, spending significant time basking to regulate body temperature.
